exemplar: Winthrop warns the Puritan colonists that their new community will be watched by the whole world as a model - their success or failure will prove whether a godly commonwealth can flourish.
The Puritans migrated to escape Archbishop Laud's persecution of nonconformists and the political turmoil of Charles I's England, seeking a place to practice their reformed faith.
Winthrop's 'city upon a hill' became a lasting American self-image: the idea that the United States has a special, exemplary mission in the world persisted long after Puritan New England.
parts: A. Briefly describe Winthrop's warning to the Puritan colonists in the excerpt.
B. Briefly explain ONE reason Puritans migrated to New England in the 1630s.
C. Briefly explain ONE longer-term effect of Winthrop's 'city upon a hill' idea on American thought.

stimulus.attribution: John Winthrop, 'A Model of Christian Charity,' sermon aboard the Arbella, 1630.
stimulus.text: For we must consider that we shall be as a city upon a hill. The eyes of all people are upon us.

exemplar: The photograph captures the shocking public failure of the space shuttle program: the spacecraft breaking apart in a fireball just over a minute after launch, watched live by millions including schoolchildren.
The disaster led to a 32-month grounding of the shuttle fleet and the Rogers Commission investigation, which blamed NASA's flawed decision-making culture as well as the failed O-ring seals.
The tragedy deepened public skepticism about big government technological promises and contributed to a shift toward private and international partners in later American spaceflight.
parts: A. Briefly describe what the photograph shows about the Challenger disaster.
B. Briefly explain ONE way the federal government responded to the disaster.
C. Briefly explain ONE longer-term effect of the disaster on the American space program.

stimulus.attribution: Described from the NASA photograph of the Space Shuttle Challenger disaster (Wikimedia Commons).
stimulus.text: The photograph shows the Space Shuttle Challenger breaking apart in a massive ball of fire and smoke high above the Florida coast, 73 seconds after liftoff on January 28, 1986. Debris trails arc outward from the explosion against a pale sky.
